**Plus the held MOOH tier — DROP, with the reason stated as a scope result, not an omission.** Oxyhydroxides are the physically correct OER phases for Fe/Co/Ni, and that is precisely why adding them now is a trap: a new structure family eight weeks out means new terminations, new convergence surfaces, new magnetic complexity, a second protocol in one 20-page report, and the immediate question "so why did you report rutile FeO₂ at all." The correct move is zero-compute: state with citations that Fe/Co/Ni rutile MO₂ are model phases with **no external comparator anywhere** — Man 2011's 24-paper compilation contains no rutile FeO₂ or CoO₂ row, and its only NiO₂ row is a reduced bridge-site surface (10.1002/cctc.201000397) — and that in this project they are **method test systems, not candidate catalysts**. That converts the weakness into an explicit scope statement, which is what a rigorous reader wants anyway.

contexts.text: UNVERIFIED/NOTES: WHAT IS SOLID. Every DOI in the findings was resolved against the Crossref REST API, and abstracts were confirmed via EuropePMC, the Semantic Scholar graph API, or arXiv — not from memory. Man 2011's methods (RPBE, Dacapo, ultrasoft PP, 350-400/500 eV, (1×2) cell, half coverage, kT = 0.1 eV, F < 0.05 eV/Å, spin-polarised for CrO2/MnO2/NiO/Co-oxides, explicit rejection of +U, and the 'MoO2 and CrO2 are not stable' sentence) and García-Mota 2011's Table 1 (Cr 6c-M 0.61 V, Mn 5c-M 0.69, Ru 0.80/0.74, Ir 0.63/0.67, and the note that only configurations under 0.8 V are tabulated, i.e. Fe/Co/Ni-doped TiO2 all exceeded 0.8 V) were read directly from the publisher PDFs already in docs/research/papers/. Feng 2025's numbers were text-extracted from the local PDF, not recalled. The Divanis ESI was downloaded from EuropePMC (PMC8157516 supplementaryFiles) and is on disk at C:\\Users\\frank\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Users-frank\\e1d7c42a-dea3-4568-b15f-d761db49ddbe\\scratchpad\\SC-011-C9SC05897D-s001.pdf with a text dump at divanis_esi.txt in the same directory. WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY. (1) The ΔE→ΔG reconstruction assumes the OOH correction is +0.40 eV. Divanis' Table SI-1 as extracted lists only the OH (+0.35) and O (+0.05) rows, so +0.40 is imported from the project's own referencing convention. Two independent consistency checks pass — Man 2011's high-coverage RuO2 reconstructs to 0.360 V with ΔG3 limiting, matching García-Mota's verbatim 'RuO2 has an OER overpotential of ≈0.4 V, with the formation of the intermediate HOO* being the potential-determining step', and IrO2 reconstructs to 0.53-0.59 V, matching the 0.54-0.58 V band docs/32 already used — but the assumption should be checked against Man 2011's own SI before any number enters a figure. (2) The DACAPO/GPAW RuO2 attribution to Halck 2014 comes from the article-number column of the Divanis compilation, and the DACAPO row is numerically identical to Man 2011's high-coverage row, so Halck may be quoting rather than recomputing it. Confirm against 10.1039/c4cp00571f before the 0.12 V code-spread claim is used; it is marked recalled-unverified for that reason. (3) Liang/Bieberle-Hütter/Brocks 2022 (0.63-0.73 V) and Nat. Commun. 14, 5365 (0.81 V) are taken from the project briefing. I confirmed both citations exist and resolved them (10.1021/acs.jpcc.1c08700, JPCC 126, 1337-1345, Liang/Bieberle-Hütter/Brocks; and 10.1038/s41467-023-41036-9, 'Stable and oxidative charged Ru enhance the acidic OER activity in two-dimensional ruthenium-iridium oxide'), but ACS and Nature both blocked full-text retrieval, so I did not independently verify the 0.63-0.73 V or 0.81 V values themselves. (4) Frydendal 2015 ChemCatChem 7, 149-154 (10.1002/cctc.201402756) is 'Enhancing Activity for the OER: The Beneficial Interaction of Gold with Manganese and Cobalt Oxides' — I did NOT verify that its MnO2 entry is rutile β-MnO2(110), so its reconstructed 0.500 V is quoted in the table but should not be called a rutile value until checked. (5) Stoerzinger 2014: only the abstract was retrievable, so the facet ORDERING ((100) more active than (110), at pH 13, correlating with cus-site density) is verified but no numeric current densities or overpotentials were extracted. (6) A search engine attributed the ChemRxiv preprint 'Unraveling fundamental activity-stability relationships in rutile oxides' (item 6904e0f8a482cba12250eeca) to Navodye & Gunasooriya, while Semantic Scholar gives Maraschin & Gauthier for the published JPCC version I cite. I could not reconcile these — ChemRxiv's API and page both returned 403. Cite only the published version (10.1021/acs.jpcc.5c08777, Maraschin & Gauthier, JPCC 130, 3803-3813, 2026) and do not quote the preprint author list. (7) I did not retrieve per-metal numeric values from Comer et al. 2022 (10.1021/acs.jpcc.2c02381, 'Unravelling Electronic Trends in O* and OH* Surface Adsorption in the MO2 Transition-Metal Oxide Series', JPCC 126, 7903-7909); the citation is verified, the contents are not, and it is the most likely source of an additional independent MO2(110) series if someone can get the SI. (8) RSC, ACS, Wiley and Nature article HTML all returned 403 to WebFetch throughout; everything here routed through Crossref, EuropePMC, Semantic Scholar, arXiv, or local PDFs. (9) No claim in this report rests on a figure read by eye — I discarded my initial figure-read estimates for Man 2011's CrO2 once the ESI table gave the underlying energies.

Gauthier (10.1021/acs.jpcc.7b02383) measured a ~0.3 eV solvation shift in c_M on rutile(110), which by Finding 5's exact lemma moves the floor η ≥ c_M/2 − 1.23 by 0.15 V — and Cr sits 9 meV above its floor. The method was published in Quantum ESPRESSO, so it transfers directly. Pre-register the non-additivity prediction: the solvation shift in c_M is ~0.3 eV at O coverage but ~0.1 eV at OH coverage, so unlike block 1A's ADDITIVE ×5 result for U × cell, solvation × coverage should FAIL additivity — register a threshold (e.g. |Δc_M(O) − Δc_M(OH)| > 0.10 eV) before running. Tripkovic (10.1021/acs.jpcc.7b07660) traces a 0.80 → 2.82 eV swing in ΔE(*O) on LaCrO3 across U = 0–5 eV to the adsorbate driving Cr from +3 toward +5, and shows HSE's α-dependence is equally strong. If the project's Cr shows the same oxidation-state change between rungs, P7 upgrades from 'a threshold was triggered' to 'U is not a spectator parameter when the adsorbate changes the metal's oxidation state' — a mechanism, a prediction for which of the other 3d metals should behave the same way, and a documented reason why switching to a hybrid would not have saved the headline.

DEAD ENDS: Do NOT open a grand-canonical / constant-potential re-run of the tier. Hörmann, Beinlich & Reuter (10.1021/acs.jpcc.3c07954) show constant-charge and constant-potential agree on differential free energies in the infinite-cell limit and are 'equally valid and precise', and a CHE-vs-CEP comparison on metal oxides reports consistent limiting potentials for OER. Worse, constant-charge is the MORE robust ensemble against capacitance and absolute-potential-alignment error — and this project has no trustworthy capacitance for a magnetic 3d oxide slab, so switching would import a new uncontrolled parameter to chase an expected null. | Do NOT run CI-NEB on all four rungs. Dickens, Kirk & Nørskov (10.1021/acs.jpcc.9b03830) find proton transfers facile and only O–O coupling rate-determining on rutile oxides, and Exner (10.1021/acscatal.0c03865) notes ab initio kinetic barriers can carry errors exceeding 500 meV — larger than the entire 0.93 V spread of tier_v2. A four-rung NEB campaign buys noise. Additionally, neb.x has NOT been tested in this build; docs/42's own discipline (run the binary, do not trust the manual) has never been applied to it. | Do NOT reach for a hybrid functional to escape the U problem. Tripkovic (10.1021/acs.jpcc.7b07660) shows the HSE exact-exchange α dependence is 'equally strong' as the U dependence and traceable to the same oxidation-state mechanism, so hybrids relocate the arbitrary parameter rather than removing it. Independently moot: libxc is NOT linked in this build. | Do NOT report a solvation number from a single hand-placed static water bilayer. Inico (10.1002/cctc.202400813) documents that static bilayers give 'sizeable deviations' versus AIMD on exactly TiO2/RuO2/IrO2(110), from bilayer rigidity and neglected partial water dissociation. A single registration is an unregistered free parameter of precisely the kind the symmetry trap taught this project to distrust — a builder choice invisible to every numerical gate. Sample configurations, or report an explicit bound. | Do NOT let 3D-RISM or ESM stand in for explicit water on the ΔG_OOH − ΔG_OH question. Implicit models systematically miss hydrogen bonding (Ringe et al. review; Demeyere & Skylaris 10.1021/acs.jpcc.4c04924), and hydrogen bonding is the entire mechanism by which solvation moves c_M and therefore the scaling floor. Also treat the missing .MOL solvent files as a sensitive parametrization choice, not as inert data — Demeyere finds water lone pairs 'crucial' to getting RISM right. | Do NOT chase the lattice-oxygen mechanism as a headline on pristine undoped rutile(110). Feng (10.1016/j.jcat.2025.115968) finds AEM dominant and LOM/OPM 'less likely' there; LOM on rutile is predominantly a doping- and covalency-tuning story and this project's slabs are undoped endmembers. Scope the caveat to Cr alone, where high M–O covalency makes AEM-only least safe, and state it rather than computing it.

DEAD ENDS: Do NOT open a grand-canonical / constant-potential re-run of the tier. Hörmann, Beinlich & Reuter (10.1021/acs.jpcc.3c07954) show constant-charge and constant-potential agree on differential free energies in the infinite-cell limit and are 'equally valid and precise', and a CHE-vs-CEP comparison on metal oxides reports consistent limiting potentials for OER. Worse, constant-charge is the MORE robust ensemble against capacitance and absolute-potential-alignment error — and this project has no trustworthy capacitance for a magnetic 3d oxide slab, so switching would import a new uncontrolled parameter to chase an expected null. | Do NOT run CI-NEB on all four rungs. Dickens, Kirk & Nørskov (10.1021/acs.jpcc.9b03830) find proton transfers facile and only O–O coupling rate-determining on rutile oxides, and Exner (10.1021/acscatal.0c03865) notes ab initio kinetic barriers can carry errors exceeding 500 meV — larger than the entire 0.93 V spread of tier_v2. A four-rung NEB campaign buys noise. Additionally, neb.x has NOT been tested in this build; docs/42's own discipline (run the binary, do not trust the manual) has never been applied to it. | Do NOT reach for a hybrid functional to escape the U problem. Tripkovic (10.1021/acs.jpcc.7b07660) shows the HSE exact-exchange α dependence is 'equally strong' as the U dependence and traceable to the same oxidation-state mechanism, so hybrids relocate the arbitrary parameter rather than removing it. Independently moot: libxc is NOT linked in this build. | Do NOT report a solvation number from a single hand-placed static water bilayer. Inico (10.1002/cctc.202400813) documents that static bilayers give 'sizeable deviations' versus AIMD on exactly TiO2/RuO2/IrO2(110), from bilayer rigidity and neglected partial water dissociation. A single registration is an unregistered free parameter of precisely the kind the symmetry trap taught this project to distrust — a builder choice invisible to every numerical gate. Sample configurations, or report an explicit bound. | Do NOT let 3D-RISM or ESM stand in for explicit water on the ΔG_OOH − ΔG_OH question. Implicit models systematically miss hydrogen bonding (Ringe et al. review; Demeyere & Skylaris 10.1021/acs.jpcc.4c04924), and hydrogen bonding is the entire mechanism by which solvation moves c_M and therefore the scaling floor. Also treat the missing .MOL solvent files as a sensitive parametrization choice, not as inert data — Demeyere finds water lone pairs 'crucial' to getting RISM right. | Do NOT chase the lattice-oxygen mechanism as a headline on pristine undoped rutile(110). Feng (10.1016/j.jcat.2025.115968) finds AEM dominant and LOM/OPM 'less likely' there; LOM on rutile is predominantly a doping- and covalency-tuning story and this project's slabs are undoped endmembers. PRB 85, 235149 (2012) built BEEF-vdW by regularised machine-learning fitting over molecular formation/reaction energies, barriers, non-covalent interactions, solid-state properties and chemisorption, deriving a probability distribution over XC parameters. The standard practice is: one self-consistent BEEF-vdW calculation, then a NON-self-consistent evaluation of ~2000 ensemble functionals on that fixed density, giving a distribution of adsorption energies whose standard deviation is the reported error bar; that sigma is then propagated to limiting potential and overpotential. The companion empirical anchor is Wellendorff et al., Surf. Sci. 640, 36 (2015), DOI 10.1016/j.susc.2015.03.023, the CE27 experimental chemisorption benchmark used to calibrate what those functional MAEs actually are.

contexts.text: WHY HERE: This is the closest published example of the thing this project IS — a rigorous audit of somebody's computational/automated discovery pipeline — and it is the model for tone. Three transferable lessons: (1) the audit was structured as an exhaustive item-by-item pass over EVERY claim, not a selection of the worst cases, which is what makes it unanswerable; do the same across all 7 endmembers x 3 adsorbates rather than showcasing Cr and Ir. (2) It documents its criteria before the verdicts. (3) It establishes that this genre is publishable and valued, which is a useful thing for a solo entrant to be able to point at when a judge asks whether a negative result is a real contribution. contexts.text: DEAD ENDS: Do NOT open a grand-canonical / constant-potential re-run of the tier. Hörmann, Beinlich & Reuter (10.1021/acs.jpcc.3c07954) show constant-charge and constant-potential agree on differential free energies in the infinite-cell limit and are 'equally valid and precise', and a CHE-vs-CEP comparison on metal oxides reports consistent limiting potentials for OER. Worse, constant-charge is the MORE robust ensemble against capacitance and absolute-potential-alignment error — and this project has no trustworthy capacitance for a magnetic 3d oxide slab, so switching would import a new uncontrolled parameter to chase an expected null. | Do NOT run CI-NEB on all four rungs. Dickens, Kirk & Nørskov (10.1021/acs.jpcc.9b03830) find proton transfers facile and only O–O coupling rate-determining on rutile oxides, and Exner (10.1021/acscatal.0c03865) notes ab initio kinetic barriers can carry errors exceeding 500 meV — larger than the entire 0.93 V spread of tier_v2. A four-rung NEB campaign buys noise. Additionally, neb.x has NOT been tested in this build; docs/42's own discipline (run the binary, do not trust the manual) has never been applied to it. | Do NOT reach for a hybrid functional to escape the U problem. Tripkovic (10.1021/acs.jpcc.7b07660) shows the HSE exact-exchange α dependence is 'equally strong' as the U dependence and traceable to the same oxidation-state mechanism, so hybrids relocate the arbitrary parameter rather than removing it. Independently moot: libxc is NOT linked in this build. | Do NOT report a solvation number from a single hand-placed static water bilayer. Inico (10.1002/cctc.202400813) documents that static bilayers give 'sizeable deviations' versus AIMD on exactly TiO2/RuO2/IrO2(110), from bilayer rigidity and neglected partial water dissociation. A single registration is an unregistered free parameter of precisely the kind the symmetry trap taught this project to distrust — a builder choice invisible to every numerical gate. Sample configurations, or report an explicit bound. | Do NOT let 3D-RISM or ESM stand in for explicit water on the ΔG_OOH − ΔG_OH question. Implicit models systematically miss hydrogen bonding (Ringe et al. review; Demeyere & Skylaris 10.1021/acs.jpcc.4c04924), and hydrogen bonding is the entire mechanism by which solvation moves c_M and therefore the scaling floor. Also treat the missing .MOL solvent files as a sensitive parametrization choice, not as inert data — Demeyere finds water lone pairs 'crucial' to getting RISM right. | Do NOT chase the lattice-oxygen mechanism as a headline on pristine undoped rutile(110). Feng (10.1016/j.jcat.2025.115968) finds AEM dominant and LOM/OPM 'less likely' there; LOM on rutile is predominantly a doping- and covalency-tuning story and this project's slabs are undoped endmembers. Scope the caveat to Cr alone, where high M–O covalency makes AEM-only least safe, and state it rather than computing it.
- [zero-compute] Grand-canonical / constant-potential DFT is very likely a NULL for this project's η — cite it, do not run it (10.1021/acs.jpcc.3c07954, confirmed-from-abstract)

8. **D10 / mechanism-scope flags. (~1 day, zero compute.)** The declared-assumptions section: AEM dominance on pristine rutile (Feng 2025, 10.1016/j.jcat.2025.115968), the CPET-vs-SPET assumption under every rung (Exner, 10.1021/acs.accounts.4c00048), the Cr covalency caveat as the one endmember where AEM-only is least safe, and grand-canonical DFT declared as an expected null with a citation rather than an unquantified hole (Hörmann 10.1021/acs.jpcc.3c07954). This is cheap insurance against the three most obvious referee questions.

contexts.text: WHAT: Urrego-Ortiz, Builes, Illas, Calle-Vallejo, EES Catal. 2, 157-179 (2024) is the review: DFT gas-phase errors (notably O2, and H2O2 for the 2e- pathway) are at least ~0.3 eV in the total energy of O2 for PW91, RPBE, PBE and BEEF-vdW alike, and they contaminate the equilibrium potential, individual step energies, scaling relations and volcano positions — not just adsorption energies. The standard detection-and-correction machinery is Granda-Marulanda et al., ACS Catal. 10, 6900 (2020), DOI 10.1021/acscatal.0c01075, a semiempirical method that pinpoints errors from formation energies and then applies sequential corrections. The volcano-with-error-bars version is Urrego-Ortiz, Almeida, Calle-Vallejo, ChemSusChem 17, e202400873 (2024), DOI 10.1002/cssc.202400873.

| 1 | Exner 2020, ACS Catal. 10, 12607 | 10.1021/acscatal.0c03865 | Gmax(η) definition; 0.20 eV ranking floor; η_TD unreliable near apex |

TOP 3: ZERO-COMPUTE, DO IT FIRST: recompute frozen tier_v2 under η_TD vs ESSI vs ESAI vs Gmax(η) from the four rungs already on disk, and re-run the existing σ = 0.35–0.40 eV Monte Carlo for each estimator. Finding 4 already proves η is a positively-biased max-statistic; this measures whether the project's own catalogued error classes (P7's 1.122 V U-swing, the 406 meV magnetic drifts, the symmetry trap's 0.291 V on Ir) propagate differently through a less noise-amplifying estimator. It needs no DFT, no box, no wall-clock, and it converts the project's sharpest theoretical result into a comparative measurement. Cites 10.1021/acscatal.0c03865 and 10.1016/j.mex.2021.101590. | THE ONE LEVER ON THE SCALING FLOOR: explicit-water solvation of *OH/*O/*OOH, targeting c_M = ΔG_OOH − ΔG_OH rather than η. Gauthier (10.1021/acs.jpcc.7b02383) measured a ~0.3 eV solvation shift in c_M on rutile(110), which by Finding 5's exact lemma moves the floor η ≥ c_M/2 − 1.23 by 0.15 V — and Cr sits 9 meV above its floor. The method was published in Quantum ESPRESSO, so it transfers directly. Pre-register the non-additivity prediction: the solvation shift in c_M is ~0.3 eV at O coverage but ~0.1 eV at OH coverage, so unlike block 1A's ADDITIVE ×5 result for U × cell, solvation × coverage should FAIL additivity — register a threshold (e.g. |Δc_M(O) − Δc_M(OH)| > 0.10 eV) before running. Guard with Inico's finding (10.1002/cctc.202400813) that a single static bilayer deviates sizeably from AIMD: sample configurations or report a bound. | EXPLAIN P7 RATHER THAN JUST REPORTING IT, at near-zero cost: run projwfc.x on the U-ladder densities already budgeted for regeneration under A5.3a and track Cr's Löwdin charge and local moment per adsorbate state. Tripkovic (10.1021/acs.jpcc.7b07660) traces a 0.80 → 2.82 eV swing in ΔE(*O) on LaCrO3 across U = 0–5 eV to the adsorbate driving Cr from +3 toward +5, and shows HSE's α-dependence is equally strong. If the project's Cr shows the same oxidation-state change between rungs, P7 upgrades from 'a threshold was triggered' to 'U is not a spectator parameter when the adsorbate changes the metal's oxidation state' — a mechanism, a prediction for which of the other 3d metals should behave the same way, and a documented reason why switching to a hybrid would not have saved the headline.

DEAD ENDS: Do NOT open a grand-canonical / constant-potential re-run of the tier. Hörmann, Beinlich & Reuter (10.1021/acs.jpcc.3c07954) show constant-charge and constant-potential agree on differential free energies in the infinite-cell limit and are 'equally valid and precise', and a CHE-vs-CEP comparison on metal oxides reports consistent limiting potentials for OER. Worse, constant-charge is the MORE robust ensemble against capacitance and absolute-potential-alignment error — and this project has no trustworthy capacitance for a magnetic 3d oxide slab, so switching would import a new uncontrolled parameter to chase an expected null. | Do NOT run CI-NEB on all four rungs. Dickens, Kirk & Nørskov (10.1021/acs.jpcc.9b03830) find proton transfers facile and only O–O coupling rate-determining on rutile oxides, and Exner (10.1021/acscatal.0c03865) notes ab initio kinetic barriers can carry errors exceeding 500 meV — larger than the entire 0.93 V spread of tier_v2. A four-rung NEB campaign buys noise. Additionally, neb.x has NOT been tested in this build; docs/42's own discipline (run the binary, do not trust the manual) has never been applied to it. | Do NOT reach for a hybrid functional to escape the U problem. Tripkovic (10.1021/acs.jpcc.7b07660) shows the HSE exact-exchange α dependence is 'equally strong' as the U dependence and traceable to the same oxidation-state mechanism, so hybrids relocate the arbitrary parameter rather than removing it. Independently moot: libxc is NOT linked in this build. | Do NOT report a solvation number from a single hand-placed static water bilayer. Inico (10.1002/cctc.202400813) documents that static bilayers give 'sizeable deviations' versus AIMD on exactly TiO2/RuO2/IrO2(110), from bilayer rigidity and neglected partial water dissociation. A single registration is an unregistered free parameter of precisely the kind the symmetry trap taught this project to distrust — a builder choice invisible to every numerical gate. Sample configurations, or report an explicit bound. | Do NOT let 3D-RISM or ESM stand in for explicit water on the ΔG_OOH − ΔG_OH question. Implicit models systematically miss hydrogen bonding (Ringe et al. review; Demeyere & Skylaris 10.1021/acs.jpcc.4c04924), and hydrogen bonding is the entire mechanism by which solvation moves c_M and therefore the scaling floor. Also treat the missing .MOL solvent files as a sensitive parametrization choice, not as inert data — Demeyere finds water lone pairs 'crucial' to getting RISM right. | Do NOT chase the lattice-oxygen mechanism as a headline on pristine undoped rutile(110). Feng (10.1016/j.jcat.2025.115968) finds AEM dominant and LOM/OPM 'less likely' there; LOM on rutile is predominantly a doping- and covalency-tuning story and this project's slabs are undoped endmembers. Scope the caveat to Cr alone, where high M–O covalency makes AEM-only least safe, and state it rather than computing it.
- [zero-compute] ESSI / ESAI / Gmax: three alternative activity estimators computable from the SAME four rungs, at literally zero new DFT (10.1021/acscatal.0c03865, confirmed-from-paper)

**Runs:** zero DFT, ~2 GPU-hours for the MLIP rescore. (a) Recompute frozen tier_v2 and tier_v3 under η_TD / ESSI / ESAI / G_max(η) — `g_max()` is already session-verified against Razzaq–Exner and reproduces docs/29 §4b exactly, so this is a day's work (10.1021/acscatal.0c03865, 10.1016/j.mex.2021.101590). (b) The floor/excess table with the **closed form registered first**: for pls ∈ {2,3}, η = (c_M/2 − 1.23) + |ΔG₂ − ΔG₃|/2, i.e. excess = |ΔG_O − (ΔG_OH + ΔG_OOH)/2|; the identity breaks when pls flips to 1 or 4, and docs/41 §6f shows Co and Ni both flipped 1→2 under correction while the LIT-1 Co ladder returns pls=1 at U=4.48 — so pls flips are live in exactly the arms this depends on. (c) The n=7 statistics repair: exact-permutation CI on ρ = 0.8929, Holm across the four heads tested (0.0123 × 4 = **0.049**, a knife-edge that must be *disclosed*, not discovered by a judge), both Ir orderings as a sensitivity pair, conclusion stated **ordinally**. Never bootstrap at n=7 (de Winter 2016, 10.1037/met0000079). (d) Prediction efficiency for the tier at the measured σ (Krishnamurthy 2018, 10.1021/acs.jpclett.7b02895) — if the tier was never resolvable, that is a far stronger closing than "the numbers moved."

2. **The estimator suite: η_TD vs ESSI vs ESAI vs G_max. (~0.5 day, zero compute.)** Registered under A5.1c; `g_max()` already verified algebraically identical to Razzaq–Exner eqs 10–25. Tests whether the project's *own* catalogued error classes propagate differently through a less noise-amplifying statistic — the 1.122 V U-swing, the 406 meV drifts, the 0.291 V Ir shift, all re-scored under four estimators. 10.1021/acscatal.0c03865; 10.1016/j.mex.2021.101590. Note the ESSI-origin citation is unresolved: cite ESAI (Exner, MethodsX 2021), which was verified.

(a) **Score P-SYMCOV and the per-metal Δη table** in their registered units, separately; publish the measured ICC and DEFF. (b) **The floor/excess decomposition** with the closed form registered first: for pls ∈ {2,3}, η = (c_M/2 − 1.23) + |ΔG₂ − ΔG₃|/2, i.e. excess = |ΔG_O − (ΔG_OH + ΔG_OOH)/2|; **the identity breaks when pls flips to 1 or 4**, and the flips are live in exactly the arms this depends on. **Report span(c_M)/2 at fixed endpoints, never max-minus-min over a grid**, and report the U at which each metal's pls flips as a deliverable in its own right. (c) **The four-estimator comparison** η_TD / ESSI / ESAI / G_max(η) with the σ Monte Carlo re-run per estimator (**10.1021/acscatal.0c03865**; cite ESAI at **10.1016/j.mex.2021.101590**, which was verified — the ESSI-origin citation is unresolved). (d) **The n = 7 statistics repair**, disclosed not discovered: exact-permutation CI on ρ = 0.8929, Holm across the four heads tested (0.0123 × 4 = **0.049**, a knife-edge), both Ir orderings (0.490 and 0.781, different ranks) as a sensitivity pair, conclusion stated **ordinally**, never bootstrapped at small n (**10.1037/met0000079**). Re-score against `tier_v3` with the **range-extension caveat stated explicitly** — TiO₂ is a d⁰ wide-gap oxide whose cus descriptor sits outside the current 0.33–1.26 V span and will inflate Spearman mechanically. (e) **Cite Krishnamurthy, Sumaria & Viswanathan (10.1021/acs.jpclett.7b02895)** for the expected-activity/prediction-efficiency framework *before* any bias wording is fixed, and claim only what is distinct: because 4.92 eV is imposed, η reduces **exactly** to max(rungs) − mean(rungs), a structural identity that is ≥ 0 by construction and monotonically inflated by error of any origin. (Note its actual title is *"Maximal Predictability Approach for Identifying the Right Descriptors for Electrocatalytic Reactions"* — attribute the "expected activity" formalism carefully, possibly to the Deshpande 2016 companion **10.1021/acscatal.6b00509**.) (f) **Write the Society's one non-technical sentence and check the results support it**; if they do not, cut a claim, not the sentence.

contexts.text: - **Toolchain & data:** OC22 oxide relaxations + EquiformerV2/GemNet-OC fine-tuning; predict adsorption descriptors → activity ranking ([OC22](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acscatal.2c05426)).
- Open Catalyst 2022 (OC22) dataset & oxide benchmarks — [arXiv:2206.08917](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.08917) and [ACS Catal.](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acscatal.2c05426)

The entire UMA campaign (screen + parity) ran `uma-s-1p1` with **`task_name="oc20"`** — the head that emulates **RPBE adsorption energies on metals**. The correct head for our chemistry is **`oc22`** (PBE+U oxide **total** energies), which only exists in the `uma-s-1p2` / `uma-s-1p2p1` checkpoints. OC22's training data (Tran et al., arXiv:2206.08917; ACS Catal. 10.1021/acscatal.2c05426) is *literally our system*: VASP PBE+U with Materials-Project U (same scheme as our QE tier), spin-polarized, **4,318 rutile systems incl. unary/binary rutiles, with O*/OH*/OOH* OER intermediates in-distribution**.

**OC22 dataset (what `oc22` emulates).** Tran et al. (Open Catalyst / CMU-Meta), 2022/2023. arXiv:**2206.08917**; ACS Catalysis DOI **10.1021/acscatal.2c05426**. https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.08917 — *verified.* 62,331 relaxations / ~9.85M single-points; **PBE + Hubbard U (Materials Project scheme; 20,812 systems used +U)**; **VASP; spin-polarized (FM/NM init per Horton et al. magnetic moments)**; **DFT total energies** (S2EF-Total, no referencing). **Explicitly includes 173 unary/binary rutile structures (4,318 rutile systems) and O*/OH*/OOH*/O₂* OER intermediates.** (OC20, by contrast, is RPBE adsorption energies.)

WHAT: Formalises propagation of adsorption-energy uncertainty through thermodynamic activity models: calculated activity is converted into a probability distribution and an EXPECTED activity is computed, rather than a point value. Introduces 'prediction efficiency' — a quantitative measure of a descriptor's ability to distinguish materials across an activity range given the uncertainty — and applies it to four reactions including OER. Companion to the already-known Deshpande/Kitchin/Viswanathan ACS Catal 6, 5251 (2016), DOI 10.1021/acscatal.6b00509, which does the ORR volcano version.

(a) **Score P-SYMCOV and the per-metal Δη table** in their registered units, separately; publish the measured ICC and DEFF. (b) **The floor/excess decomposition** with the closed form registered first: for pls ∈ {2,3}, η = (c_M/2 − 1.23) + |ΔG₂ − ΔG₃|/2, i.e. excess = |ΔG_O − (ΔG_OH + ΔG_OOH)/2|; **the identity breaks when pls flips to 1 or 4**, and the flips are live in exactly the arms this depends on. **Report span(c_M)/2 at fixed endpoints, never max-minus-min over a grid**, and report the U at which each metal's pls flips as a deliverable in its own right. (c) **The four-estimator comparison** η_TD / ESSI / ESAI / G_max(η) with the σ Monte Carlo re-run per estimator (**10.1021/acscatal.0c03865**; cite ESAI at **10.1016/j.mex.2021.101590**, which was verified — the ESSI-origin citation is unresolved). (d) **The n = 7 statistics repair**, disclosed not discovered: exact-permutation CI on ρ = 0.8929, Holm across the four heads tested (0.0123 × 4 = **0.049**, a knife-edge), both Ir orderings (0.490 and 0.781, different ranks) as a sensitivity pair, conclusion stated **ordinally**, never bootstrapped at small n (**10.1037/met0000079**). Re-score against `tier_v3` with the **range-extension caveat stated explicitly** — TiO₂ is a d⁰ wide-gap oxide whose cus descriptor sits outside the current 0.33–1.26 V span and will inflate Spearman mechanically. (e) **Cite Krishnamurthy, Sumaria & Viswanathan (10.1021/acs.jpclett.7b02895)** for the expected-activity/prediction-efficiency framework *before* any bias wording is fixed, and claim only what is distinct: because 4.92 eV is imposed, η reduces **exactly** to max(rungs) − mean(rungs), a structural identity that is ≥ 0 by construction and monotonically inflated by error of any origin. (Note its actual title is *"Maximal Predictability Approach for Identifying the Right Descriptors for Electrocatalytic Reactions"* — attribute the "expected activity" formalism carefully, possibly to the Deshpande 2016 companion **10.1021/acscatal.6b00509**.) (f) **Write the Society's one non-technical sentence and check the results support it**; if they do not, cut a claim, not the sentence.

contexts.text: | ORR (fuel-cell cathode) | Half-wave potential E₁/₂; mass activity | Pt-group dominance vs. cost; HEA/single-atom sites break scaling ([JACS 2024](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/jacs.3c14486)) |

The field is governed by **linear scaling relations**: on a given surface the binding energies of reaction intermediates (e.g., *OH, *O, *OOH in OER) are mechanistically correlated, so you cannot independently tune them. This forces every conventional catalyst onto a **volcano plot** and imposes a hard floor — the best-case OER thermodynamic overpotential is **~0.37 V**, versus the ~0.0 V you'd get if each step were individually ideal ([Frontiers, Sabatier review](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/energy-research/articles/10.3389/fenrg.2021.654460/full); [Chem. Soc. Rev. 2025](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2025/cs/d5cs00597c)). Real progress means **circumventing scaling relations**, which is exactly why HEAs and single-atom catalysts are hot: their disordered, multi-element active-site distributions can break the correlations that cap conventional alloys ([JACS 2024 HEA-ORR](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/jacs.3c14486); [Nat. Commun. 2023, "unusual Sabatier on HEA"](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-44261-4)).

| HEA composition active learning | Multi-objective Bayesian optimization over composition space (activity + cost + entropic stability); diversity-batched — proven on 4.3×10¹² HEA candidates ([JACS 2024](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/jacs.3c14486)) | Med (your existing alloy-design + active-learning stack maps directly) |

Every DOI in the findings was resolved against the Crossref REST API, and abstracts were confirmed via EuropePMC, the Semantic Scholar graph API, or arXiv — not from memory. Man 2011's methods (RPBE, Dacapo, ultrasoft PP, 350-400/500 eV, (1×2) cell, half coverage, kT = 0.1 eV, F < 0.05 eV/Å, spin-polarised for CrO2/MnO2/NiO/Co-oxides, explicit rejection of +U, and the 'MoO2 and CrO2 are not stable' sentence) and García-Mota 2011's Table 1 (Cr 6c-M 0.61 V, Mn 5c-M 0.69, Ru 0.80/0.74, Ir 0.63/0.67, and the note that only configurations under 0.8 V are tabulated, i.e. Fe/Co/Ni-doped TiO2 all exceeded 0.8 V) were read directly from the publisher PDFs already in docs/research/papers/. Feng 2025's numbers were text-extracted from the local PDF, not recalled. The Divanis ESI was downloaded from EuropePMC (PMC8157516 supplementaryFiles) and is on disk at C:\\Users\\frank\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Users-frank\\e1d7c42a-dea3-4568-b15f-d761db49ddbe\\scratchpad\\SC-011-C9SC05897D-s001.pdf with a text dump at divanis_esi.txt in the same directory. WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY. (1) The ΔE→ΔG reconstruction assumes the OOH correction is +0.40 eV. Divanis' Table SI-1 as extracted lists only the OH (+0.35) and O (+0.05) rows, so +0.40 is imported from the project's own referencing convention. Two independent consistency checks pass — Man 2011's high-coverage RuO2 reconstructs to 0.360 V with ΔG3 limiting, matching García-Mota's verbatim 'RuO2 has an OER overpotential of ≈0.4 V, with the formation of the intermediate HOO* being the potential-determining step', and IrO2 reconstructs to 0.53-0.59 V, matching the 0.54-0.58 V band docs/32 already used — but the assumption should be checked against Man 2011's own SI before any number enters a figure. (2) The DACAPO/GPAW RuO2 attribution to Halck 2014 comes from the article-number column of the Divanis compilation, and the DACAPO row is numerically identical to Man 2011's high-coverage row, so Halck may be quoting rather than recomputing it. contexts.text: 2. **Any screening claim must be gated by aqueous stability.** The standard framework: computed Pourbaix ΔG_pbx (Persson et al., PRB 2012, 10.1103/PhysRevB.85.235438; Wang et al., npj Comput. Mater. 2020, 10.1038/s41524-020-00430-3 — both live in the Materials Project Pourbaix app, i.e., mostly free to us). The modern template that does activity+stability+cost jointly with an OC22 model is Tran et al. 2024 (arXiv:2311.00784, Nanoscale 10.1039/d4nr01390e) — 4,119 oxides screened. That paper is the blueprint for our funnel.

- **C0b. Wang, Guo, Montoya, Persson (2020),** "Predicting aqueous stability of solid with computed Pourbaix diagram using SCAN functional," *npj Computational Materials* 6:160. **DOI 10.1038/s41524-020-00430-3.** OA preprint (ChemRxiv): https://chemrxiv.org/engage/chemrxiv/article-details/60c74f124c8919eafdad3b3a [SEARCH]. Defines the **Pourbaix decomposition energy (ΔG_pbx)** metric and adds **SCAN+U** corrections for TM oxides — the recommended stability filter for a screening project.

DEAD ENDS: DO NOT audit OC20 for the symmetry trap. Verified from fairchem's own source (src/fairchem/data/oc/utils/vasp_flags.py): the slab/adslab VASP_FLAGS set isym=0 and symprec=1e-10, so symmetry is explicitly disabled and no exact-zero forces can appear. Use OC20 only as the detector's negative control. (Its ispin=1 across 1.28M relaxations is separately quotable as a silent approximation, but OC20 is metals with C/N/O chemistry, not oxide OER.) | DO NOT reach for ODAC23, OMol25, or OMC25. Wrong domain entirely — MOF/gas-capture, isolated molecules at wB97M-V/def2-TZVPD, and molecular crystals respectively. None contain OER intermediates on oxide slabs, so none can host a symmetry, magnetic-basin, or scaling-floor audit. Their size is seductive and irrelevant. | DO NOT treat AFLOW, OQMD, or Alexandria as adsorption-energy sources. They are bulk-crystal databases with no slabs and no adsorbates; Alexandria is 415k bulk materials at PBE/PBEsol/SCAN. They are useful for exactly one thing here — E_hull / convex-hull stability gating of the expanded rutile tier — and nothing else. Likewise Materials Project's surface database (Crystalium, 10.1038/sdata.2016.80) covers ELEMENTAL crystals only, so it cannot supply a single oxide slab; use MP for Pourbaix (10.1103/PhysRevB.85.235438, SCAN variant 10.1038/s41524-020-00430-3) instead. | DO NOT resurrect MLIP fine-tuning on OC22 or on the Xu geometries as a way to exploit the new data. The original kill reason still holds (all candidate training frames have F_y == 0, i.e. zero signal on the coordinate the trap lives in) — and the Xu deposit makes it WORSE, since its adsorbate frames are symmetry-locked too, so it would add thousands more frames carrying the identical blind spot. arXiv 2601.21056 adds an independent reason: selective +U in MPtrj/Alexandria/OMat24 produces spurious metal-oxygen repulsion in fine-tuned oxide models. | DO NOT expand the reference tier with more fictitious 3d rutiles to chase n. The repo's own stability survey establishes that FeO2 needs >74 GPa, CoO2/NiO2 are layered not rutile, CuO2 does not exist, and CrO2 dissolves as chromate at OER potentials. Adding VO2/TaO2/OsO2 (real) is defensible; adding ScO2/TiO2-analogue 3d fictions to reach n=12 multiplies numbers for phases that are not electrodes and hands a reviewer the easiest possible objection. | DO NOT launch the OC22 symmetry audit before reading OC22's actual ISYM setting. OC20's isym=0 does NOT transfer — OC22 followed Materials Project conventions, and pymatgen's MP input sets do not override VASP's ISYM=2 default. If OC22 ran with symmetry on, the audit is the biggest result available; if it ran isym=0, the arm is empty. Read it from the OC22 SI or from a downloaded trajectory's stored calculator parameters FIRST, and make that a gate in the pre-registration rather than an assumption inside it.

Energy-above-hull is a weak proxy for synthesizability; metastable-but-real and stable-but-never-synthesized materials both break the assumption ([*Nat. Commun.* 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-61778-y); synthesizability-guided pipeline [arXiv:2511.01790](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.01790v1)). The cautionary tale: GNoME predicted ~380k "stable" candidates ([*Nature* 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06735-9](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06735-9)) and the paired A-Lab claimed 41 autonomous syntheses ([*Nature* 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06734-w](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06734-w)) — then outside chemists (Palgrave et al.) argued few if any were genuinely new phases ([Chemistry World](https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/new-analysis-raises-doubts-over-autonomous-labs-materials-discoveries/4018791.article)). **A single real experimental confirmation is worth more than 10,000 generated candidates** — and that is precisely the student's structural advantage.

Its 2024 successor, Bosoni et al., Nat. Rev. Phys. 6, 45 (2024), DOI 10.1038/s42254-023-00655-3, extends this to 960 equations of state covering Z = 1-96 (unaries and oxides) with AiiDA common workflows and all-electron references. The precursor is Lejaeghere et al., Crit. Rev. Solid State Mater. Sci. 39, 1 (2014), DOI 10.1080/10408436.2013.772503. The one step toward surfaces is De Waele, Lejaeghere, Sluydts, Cottenier, PRB 94, 235418 (2016), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevB.94.235418, which puts error bars on surface energy and work function (work functions accurate to <0.3 eV) — still no adsorbates, no oxide slabs, no reaction free energies.

contexts.text: DEAD ENDS: DO NOT audit OC20 for the symmetry trap. Verified from fairchem's own source (src/fairchem/data/oc/utils/vasp_flags.py): the slab/adslab VASP_FLAGS set isym=0 and symprec=1e-10, so symmetry is explicitly disabled and no exact-zero forces can appear. Use OC20 only as the detector's negative control. (Its ispin=1 across 1.28M relaxations is separately quotable as a silent approximation, but OC20 is metals with C/N/O chemistry, not oxide OER.) | DO NOT reach for ODAC23, OMol25, or OMC25. Wrong domain entirely — MOF/gas-capture, isolated molecules at wB97M-V/def2-TZVPD, and molecular crystals respectively. None contain OER intermediates on oxide slabs, so none can host a symmetry, magnetic-basin, or scaling-floor audit. Their size is seductive and irrelevant. | DO NOT treat AFLOW, OQMD, or Alexandria as adsorption-energy sources. They are bulk-crystal databases with no slabs and no adsorbates; Alexandria is 415k bulk materials at PBE/PBEsol/SCAN. They are useful for exactly one thing here — E_hull / convex-hull stability gating of the expanded rutile tier — and nothing else. Likewise Materials Project's surface database (Crystalium, 10.1038/sdata.2016.80) covers ELEMENTAL crystals only, so it cannot supply a single oxide slab; use MP for Pourbaix (10.1103/PhysRevB.85.235438, SCAN variant 10.1038/s41524-020-00430-3) instead. | DO NOT resurrect MLIP fine-tuning on OC22 or on the Xu geometries as a way to exploit the new data. The original kill reason still holds (all candidate training frames have F_y == 0, i.e. zero signal on the coordinate the trap lives in) — and the Xu deposit makes it WORSE, since its adsorbate frames are symmetry-locked too, so it would add thousands more frames carrying the identical blind spot. arXiv 2601.21056 adds an independent reason: selective +U in MPtrj/Alexandria/OMat24 produces spurious metal-oxygen repulsion in fine-tuned oxide models. | DO NOT expand the reference tier with more fictitious 3d rutiles to chase n. The repo's own stability survey establishes that FeO2 needs >74 GPa, CoO2/NiO2 are layered not rutile, CuO2 does not exist, and CrO2 dissolves as chromate at OER potentials. Adding VO2/TaO2/OsO2 (real) is defensible; adding ScO2/TiO2-analogue 3d fictions to reach n=12 multiplies numbers for phases that are not electrodes and hands a reviewer the easiest possible objection. | DO NOT launch the OC22 symmetry audit before reading OC22's actual ISYM setting. OC20's isym=0 does NOT transfer — OC22 followed Materials Project conventions, and pymatgen's MP input sets do not override VASP's ISYM=2 default. If OC22 ran with symmetry on, the audit is the biggest result available; if it ran isym=0, the arm is empty. Read it from the OC22 SI or from a downloaded trajectory's stored calculator parameters FIRST, and make that a gate in the pre-registration rather than an assumption inside it.

UNVERIFIED/NOTES: WHAT IS SOLID. Every DOI in the findings was resolved against the Crossref REST API, and abstracts were confirmed via EuropePMC, the Semantic Scholar graph API, or arXiv — not from memory. Man 2011's methods (RPBE, Dacapo, ultrasoft PP, 350-400/500 eV, (1×2) cell, half coverage, kT = 0.1 eV, F < 0.05 eV/Å, spin-polarised for CrO2/MnO2/NiO/Co-oxides, explicit rejection of +U, and the 'MoO2 and CrO2 are not stable' sentence) and García-Mota 2011's Table 1 (Cr 6c-M 0.61 V, Mn 5c-M 0.69, Ru 0.80/0.74, Ir 0.63/0.67, and the note that only configurations under 0.8 V are tabulated, i.e. Fe/Co/Ni-doped TiO2 all exceeded 0.8 V) were read directly from the publisher PDFs already in docs/research/papers/. Feng 2025's numbers were text-extracted from the local PDF, not recalled. The Divanis ESI was downloaded from EuropePMC (PMC8157516 supplementaryFiles) and is on disk at C:\\Users\\frank\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Users-frank\\e1d7c42a-dea3-4568-b15f-d761db49ddbe\\scratchpad\\SC-011-C9SC05897D-s001.pdf with a text dump at divanis_esi.txt in the same directory. WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY. (1) The ΔE→ΔG reconstruction assumes the OOH correction is +0.40 eV. Divanis' Table SI-1 as extracted lists only the OH (+0.35) and O (+0.05) rows, so +0.40 is imported from the project's own referencing convention. Two independent consistency checks pass — Man 2011's high-coverage RuO2 reconstructs to 0.360 V with ΔG3 limiting, matching García-Mota's verbatim 'RuO2 has an OER overpotential of ≈0.4 V, with the formation of the intermediate HOO* being the potential-determining step', and IrO2 reconstructs to 0.53-0.59 V, matching the 0.54-0.58 V band docs/32 already used — but the assumption should be checked against Man 2011's own SI before any number enters a figure. (2) The DACAPO/GPAW RuO2 attribution to Halck 2014 comes from the article-number column of the Divanis compilation, and the DACAPO row is numerically identical to Man 2011's high-coverage row, so Halck may be quoting rather than recomputing it. Confirm against 10.1039/c4cp00571f before the 0.12 V code-spread claim is used; it is marked recalled-unverified for that reason. (3) Liang/Bieberle-Hütter/Brocks 2022 (0.63-0.73 V) and Nat. Commun. 14, 5365 (0.81 V) are taken from the project briefing. I confirmed both citations exist and resolved them (10.1021/acs.jpcc.1c08700, JPCC 126, 1337-1345, Liang/Bieberle-Hütter/Brocks; and 10.1038/s41467-023-41036-9, 'Stable and oxidative charged Ru enhance the acidic OER activity in two-dimensional ruthenium-iridium oxide'), but ACS and Nature both blocked full-text retrieval, so I did not independently verify the 0.63-0.73 V or 0.81 V values themselves. (4) Frydendal 2015 ChemCatChem 7, 149-154 (10.1002/cctc.201402756) is 'Enhancing Activity for the OER: The Beneficial Interaction of Gold with Manganese and Cobalt Oxides' — I did NOT verify that its MnO2 entry is rutile β-MnO2(110), so its reconstructed 0.500 V is quoted in the table but should not be called a rutile value until checked. (5) Stoerzinger 2014: only the abstract was retrievable, so the facet ORDERING ((100) more active than (110), at pH 13, correlating with cus-site density) is verified but no numeric current densities or overpotentials were extracted. (6) A search engine attributed the ChemRxiv preprint 'Unraveling fundamental activity-stability relationships in rutile oxides' (item 6904e0f8a482cba12250eeca) to Navodye & Gunasooriya, while Semantic Scholar gives Maraschin & Gauthier for the published JPCC version I cite. I could not reconcile these — ChemRxiv's API and page both returned 403. Cite only the published version (10.1021/acs.jpcc.5c08777, Maraschin & Gauthier, JPCC 130, 3803-3813, 2026) and do not quote the preprint author list. (7) I did not retrieve per-metal numeric values from Comer et al. 2022 (10.1021/acs.jpcc.2c02381, 'Unravelling Electronic Trends in O* and OH* Surface Adsorption in the MO2 Transition-Metal Oxide Series', JPCC 126, 7903-7909); the citation is verified, the contents are not, and it is the most likely source of an additional independent MO2(110) series if someone can get the SI. (8) RSC, ACS, Wiley and Nature article HTML all returned 403 to WebFetch throughout; everything here routed through Crossref, EuropePMC, Semantic Scholar, arXiv, or local PDFs. (9) No claim in this report rests on a figure read by eye — I discarded my initial figure-read estimates for Man 2011's CrO2 once the ESI table gave the underlying energies.

contexts.text: 1. **The Co/Cu SCF failures were physics, not tuning.** Rutile CoO₂/CuO₂ are electronically frustrated fictitious phases; two solvers finding different self-consistent spin states at identical coordinates is what that looks like. Reframe from "failed jobs" to "the calculation diagnosing an unphysical phase" — with the published cures (occupation-matrix control, U-ramping, quasi-annealing; Allen & Watson, PCCP 2014, 10.1039/C4CP01083C) available if we still want converged model values.

Rutile DFT practice: Xu/Kitchin 2015 (10.1021/jp511426q) · Lim 2021 (10.3389/fenrg.2021.606313, OA) · Swathilakshmi 2023 r2SCAN+U (10.1021/acs.jctc.3c00030) · García-Mota 2012 Co+U (10.1021/jp306303y) · Allen & Watson OMC 2014 (10.1039/C4CP01083C) · Liang AFM-RuO₂ 2022 (10.1021/acs.jpcc.1c08700).

**B7. Allen, Watson (2014). "Occupation matrix control of d- and f-electron localisations using DFT+U."** *Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys.* 16(39), 21016–21031. DOI: **10.1039/C4CP01083C**. OA PDF: [SciSpace](https://scispace.com/pdf/occupation-matrix-control-of-d-and-f-electron-localisations-37xxf0ys6b.pdf); VASP tool: [WatsonGroupTCD/Occupation-matrix-control-in-VASP](https://github.com/WatsonGroupTCD/Occupation-matrix-control-in-VASP).

2. **Fix magnetic multistability with occupation-matrix control / U-ramping / quasi-annealing, and initialize each slab from its correct bulk magnetic ground state** (CrO₂ FM half-metal, β-MnO₂ AFM, test FM/AFM for Co/Ni/Cu). Backing: Allen & Watson 2014 (10.1039/C4CP01083C + VASP OMC tool), Liang 2022 (10.1021/acs.jpcc.1c08700), Lim 2021 magnetic conventions. *Cost: moderate — this is what rescues the Co and Cu endmembers.*
- [moderate] Occupation matrix control is the validated fix for Claim B — and it already exists inside your installed QE build (10.1039/c4cp01083c, confirmed-from-abstract)

Do **not** run it as a separate grid on tier_v2's 1×1 geometries, which S3 is replacing. It becomes: GATE-1 fresh-density restart on every `tier_v3` final geometry (already in S3) + two spin seeds. Add **one** occupation-matrix-controlled seed on Cr and one other metal using QE's own `starting_ns_eigenvalue` — this *is* Allen & Watson's method (10.1039/c4cp01083c), already shipped in the installed build, cheaper and more principled than a random-perturbation ensemble. Cite Qiu 2025 (10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01520, single author — "Qiu (2025)", not "et al.") as the published alternative **not** run, and say so. **Never claim discovery of DFT+U multistability:** Dorado 2009 (10.1103/PhysRevB.79.235125), **Rabone & Krack** 2013 on UO₂ *surfaces* (10.1016/j.commatsci.2013.01.023 — the digest twice misattributes this to "Dorado et al."; Critic 3 verified the authors via Crossref, and this is exactly the wrong-paper error class that has burned this campaign), Meredig 2010 (10.1103/PhysRevB.82.195128), Keshavarz & Thunström (arXiv:1810.10393, covering NiO/CoO/FeO — three of six endmembers), and Fahmy (arXiv:2509.05909) all precede it. Claim B survives only on the **mechanism** (the basin is chosen at ionic step 1 and dragged to the final geometry by `pot_extrapolation='atomic'`) and the **consequence** (a measured shift in a CHE overpotential).

Re-analysing that public dataset for imaginary-mode incidence, stratified by whether the adsorbate sits on a site-symmetry element, converts your headline from an assertion into a measurement for zero DFT hours. Three separate things already own pieces of it: Goniakowski & Gillan 1996 (10.1016/0039-6028(95)01252-4) states the physics on this exact surface family; Malyi & Zunger (10.1063/5.0015322) owns the generic 'imposed symmetry silently corrupts DFT' thesis; and the Open Catalyst production workflow hard-codes isym=0 AND symprec=1e-10, proving the field's largest dataset builders already knew. The surviving claim is not 'this error is unknown' — it is 'the correct practice has been published since 1996, the flagship dataset silently enforces it, no individual OER screen reports it, and it is invisible to every gate they DO report, worth 0.291 V on Ir.' State it that way and it is unassailable; state it any broader and a knowledgeable judge kills it in the interview. | CLAIM B'S METASTABILITY HALF IS DEAD; ITS PATH-DEPENDENCE HALF IS THE REAL FINDING. But an arXiv query on abs:'metastable' AND abs:'DFT+U' AND abs:'geometry optimization' returns ZERO results, and QE's own manual concedes that starting_ns_eigenvalue is needed 'when the default choice takes another path.' Relocate Claim B entirely onto the mechanism (the basin is selected at ionic step 1 and transported to the final geometry by pot_extrapolation='atomic') and onto the consequence (a measured overpotential shift on a catalytic surface). Cite the UO2 literature as what you are extending, never as what you are beating.

Four search strategies found no paper that re-runs published computed overpotentials and counts how many change — and Wander/Kitchin (10.1021/acs.jpcc.4c07477) have already put 4,599 DFT numerical Hessians on relaxed OC20 structures into the public domain, found imaginary modes, and discarded them as finite-difference noise without ever reporting the fraction. Re-analysing that public dataset for imaginary-mode incidence, stratified by whether the adsorbate sits on a site-symmetry element, converts your headline from an assertion into a measurement for zero DFT hours. Pre-register the threshold before downloading. | CLAIM A MUST BE NARROWED OR IT DIES. Three separate things already own pieces of it: Goniakowski & Gillan 1996 (10.1016/0039-6028(95)01252-4) states the physics on this exact surface family; Malyi & Zunger (10.1063/5.0015322) owns the generic 'imposed symmetry silently corrupts DFT' thesis; and the Open Catalyst production workflow hard-codes isym=0 AND symprec=1e-10, proving the field's largest dataset builders already knew. The surviving claim is not 'this error is unknown' — it is 'the correct practice has been published since 1996, the flagship dataset silently enforces it, no individual OER screen reports it, and it is invisible to every gate they DO report, worth 0.291 V on Ir.' State it that way and it is unassailable; state it any broader and a knowledgeable judge kills it in the interview. | CLAIM B'S METASTABILITY HALF IS DEAD; ITS PATH-DEPENDENCE HALF IS THE REAL FINDING. Dorado et al. did DFT+U metastability on UO2 SURFACES in 2013 (10.1016/j.commatsci.2013.01.023) and fused metastability with symmetry breaking in 2009 (10.1103/PhysRevB.79.235125); Allen & Watson, Meredig, Keshavarz and a 2025 JCTC paper cover the fixes. But an arXiv query on abs:'metastable' AND abs:'DFT+U' AND abs:'geometry optimization' returns ZERO results, and QE's own manual concedes that starting_ns_eigenvalue is needed 'when the default choice takes another path.' Relocate Claim B entirely onto the mechanism (the basin is selected at ionic step 1 and transported to the final geometry by pot_extrapolation='atomic') and onto the consequence (a measured overpotential shift on a catalytic surface). Cite the UO2 literature as what you are extending, never as what you are beating.

Do **not** run it as a separate grid on tier_v2's 1×1 geometries, which S3 is replacing. It becomes: GATE-1 fresh-density restart on every `tier_v3` final geometry (already in S3) + two spin seeds. Add **one** occupation-matrix-controlled seed on Cr and one other metal using QE's own `starting_ns_eigenvalue` — this *is* Allen & Watson's method (10.1039/c4cp01083c), already shipped in the installed build, cheaper and more principled than a random-perturbation ensemble. Cite Qiu 2025 (10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01520, single author — "Qiu (2025)", not "et al.") as the published alternative **not** run, and say so. **Never claim discovery of DFT+U multistability:** Dorado 2009 (10.1103/PhysRevB.79.235125), **Rabone & Krack** 2013 on UO₂ *surfaces* (10.1016/j.commatsci.2013.01.023 — the digest twice misattributes this to "Dorado et al."; Critic 3 verified the authors via Crossref, and this is exactly the wrong-paper error class that has burned this campaign), Meredig 2010 (10.1103/PhysRevB.82.195128), Keshavarz & Thunström (arXiv:1810.10393, covering NiO/CoO/FeO — three of six endmembers), and Fahmy (arXiv:2509.05909) all precede it. Claim B survives only on the **mechanism** (the basin is chosen at ionic step 1 and dragged to the final geometry by `pot_extrapolation='atomic'`) and the **consequence** (a measured shift in a CHE overpotential).

**Two corrections of record:** `starting_ns_eigenvalue` is an **initial guess on the first DFT+U iteration, NOT a constraint held through the SCF** — strictly weaker than VASP's occupation-matrix control and it must not be called OMC. And **never claim discovery of DFT+U multistability**: Dorado 2009 (**10.1103/PhysRevB.79.235125**), **Rabone & Krack** 2013 on UO₂ *surfaces* (**10.1016/j.commatsci.2013.01.023** — the digest twice misattributes this to "Dorado et al."; the authors are Jeremy Rabone and Matthias Krack), Meredig 2010 (**10.1103/PhysRevB.82.195128**), Allen & Watson (**10.1039/c4cp01083c**), Keshavarz & Thunström (**arXiv:1810.10393**, covering NiO/CoO/FeO), Qiu 2025 (**10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01520**, single author — "Qiu (2025)", not "et al."), and Fahmy (**arXiv:2509.05909**) all precede it. DEAD ENDS: DO NOT audit OC20 for the symmetry trap. Verified from fairchem's own source (src/fairchem/data/oc/utils/vasp_flags.py): the slab/adslab VASP_FLAGS set isym=0 and symprec=1e-10, so symmetry is explicitly disabled and no exact-zero forces can appear. Use OC20 only as the detector's negative control. (Its ispin=1 across 1.28M relaxations is separately quotable as a silent approximation, but OC20 is metals with C/N/O chemistry, not oxide OER.) | DO NOT reach for ODAC23, OMol25, or OMC25. Wrong domain entirely — MOF/gas-capture, isolated molecules at wB97M-V/def2-TZVPD, and molecular crystals respectively. None contain OER intermediates on oxide slabs, so none can host a symmetry, magnetic-basin, or scaling-floor audit. Their size is seductive and irrelevant. | DO NOT treat AFLOW, OQMD, or Alexandria as adsorption-energy sources. They are bulk-crystal databases with no slabs and no adsorbates; Alexandria is 415k bulk materials at PBE/PBEsol/SCAN. They are useful for exactly one thing here — E_hull / convex-hull stability gating of the expanded rutile tier — and nothing else. Likewise Materials Project's surface database (Crystalium, 10.1038/sdata.2016.80) covers ELEMENTAL crystals only, so it cannot supply a single oxide slab; use MP for Pourbaix (10.1103/PhysRevB.85.235438, SCAN variant 10.1038/s41524-020-00430-3) instead. | DO NOT resurrect MLIP fine-tuning on OC22 or on the Xu geometries as a way to exploit the new data. The original kill reason still holds (all candidate training frames have F_y == 0, i.e. zero signal on the coordinate the trap lives in) — and the Xu deposit makes it WORSE, since its adsorbate frames are symmetry-locked too, so it would add thousands more frames carrying the identical blind spot. arXiv 2601.21056 adds an independent reason: selective +U in MPtrj/Alexandria/OMat24 produces spurious metal-oxygen repulsion in fine-tuned oxide models. | DO NOT expand the reference tier with more fictitious 3d rutiles to chase n. The repo's own stability survey establishes that FeO2 needs >74 GPa, CoO2/NiO2 are layered not rutile, CuO2 does not exist, and CrO2 dissolves as chromate at OER potentials. Adding VO2/TaO2/OsO2 (real) is defensible; adding ScO2/TiO2-analogue 3d fictions to reach n=12 multiplies numbers for phases that are not electrodes and hands a reviewer the easiest possible objection. | DO NOT launch the OC22 symmetry audit before reading OC22's actual ISYM setting. OC20's isym=0 does NOT transfer — OC22 followed Materials Project conventions, and pymatgen's MP input sets do not override VASP's ISYM=2 default. If OC22 ran with symmetry on, the audit is the biggest result available; if it ran isym=0, the arm is empty. Read it from the OC22 SI or from a downloaded trajectory's stored calculator parameters FIRST, and make that a gate in the pre-registration rather than an assumption inside it.

So the defensible wording is "linear-response U determination has been industrialised across 2,000+ bulk transition-metal oxides; no published campaign applies DFPT/`hp.x` to a slab at all," which is stronger than the version currently written and is verifiable. ~45 box-h, 1.5 human-days.

contexts.text: | OER (O₂ evolution, water-splitting anode) | Overpotential @ 10 mA cm⁻²; stability @ 100+ h | Scaling relations cap thermodynamic overpotential at ~0.37 V; acid OER still needs Ir; alkaline NiFe-LDH ~250–350 mV ([Sabatier review](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/energy-research/articles/10.3389/fenrg.2021.654460/full); [Nat. Commun. 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-61356-2)) |

The field is governed by **linear scaling relations**: on a given surface the binding energies of reaction intermediates (e.g., *OH, *O, *OOH in OER) are mechanistically correlated, so you cannot independently tune them. This forces every conventional catalyst onto a **volcano plot** and imposes a hard floor — the best-case OER thermodynamic overpotential is **~0.37 V**, versus the ~0.0 V you'd get if each step were individually ideal ([Frontiers, Sabatier review](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/energy-research/articles/10.3389/fenrg.2021.654460/full); [Chem. Soc. Rev. 2025](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2025/cs/d5cs00597c)). Real progress means **circumventing scaling relations**, which is exactly why HEAs and single-atom catalysts are hot: their disordered, multi-element active-site distributions can break the correlations that cap conventional alloys ([JACS 2024 HEA-ORR](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/jacs.3c14486); [Nat. Commun. 2023, "unusual Sabatier on HEA"](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-44261-4)).
- Sabatier principle, scaling relations & the ~0.37 V OER floor — [Frontiers Energy Res. 2021](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/energy-research/articles/10.3389/fenrg.2021.654460/full)

TOP 3: AUDIT AND REPAIR THE XU 2015 DEPOSIT. It is Quantum ESPRESSO, publicly deposited (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.12635, CC0), 6,989 files, and I verified from its own force output that 40/40 sampled adsorbate relaxations ran with a non-trivial symmetry group and that *O is pinned in BOTH lateral directions (F_x = F_y = 0.00000000 exactly), *OH in one, *OOH in the orthogonal one. Phase 1 is zero-compute: parse all 810 Eads outputs plus the 680-job U ladder (10 rutiles x 4 states x 17 U points, 0.0-8.0 eV) and report the symmetry-lock census, the eta(U) spread per metal, and the scaling floor c_M/2 - 1.23 per metal. Phase 2 is the flagship compute arm: re-run the same decks at Xu's own published parameters (33/51 atoms, ecutwfc 40 / ecutrho 500, GBRV USPP, 4x4x1) with nosym=.true. and off-plane starts, and report Delta-eta(M) and Delta-eta(M,U) for 10 real rutiles. That is a like-for-like replication-and-repair of the field's canonical linear-response DFT+U rutile OER paper, with every input parameter known, and it takes the symmetry trap from n=2 (Ru, Ir) to n=10 including all five 3d metals the project has never tested. | MAKE THE ADSORBATE SEARCH DEFENSIBLE AT THE FIELD'S OWN STANDARD, MLIP-FIRST AND DFT-VERIFIED. AdsorbML's benchmark is ~100 configurations per surface across ~1,000 surfaces, with 87.36% global-minimum recovery at ~2000x speedup; against that, one placement per site is indefensible and 'we restarted off-plane' is only the second rung of a four-rung ladder. Use UMA's omat head and MACE-MPA-0 AS-IS (no fine-tuning, so the killed arm stays killed) to relax ~100 placements per (metal, adsorbate) over the expanded real-rutile tier, then verify the top-k in QE. Two things fall out for free: the fraction of the ensemble that the mirror-locked geometry actually represents, and whether the off-plane repair reached the global minimum or merely a better saddle-adjacent basin.
